newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB - Ukraine farms doubt state buying ability.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Ukraine farms doubt state buying ability.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
UKRAINIAN FARM PRODUCERS HOSTAGE TO LATE, LOW STATE BUYING
KIEV, March 27 - Ukrainian farm producers are sceptical of the government's ability to fulfil its obligations to buy grain from the 1996 and 1997 harvests.
The government still owes 100 million hryvnias, or $54 million, for grain already delivered from last year's harvest.
Even if Khlib Ukrainy, the state grain procurement agency, were to pre-pay for deliveries, it would in effect amount only to payment for previous, overdue contracts.
Any advance payments to farmers will be in the form of in-kind supplies (fuel, spare parts for farm equipment), and will done at less favourable exchange terms.
By February 23, 1997, Khlib Ukrainy had contracted for only 2.50 million tonnes of food grain out of a targeted 5.88 million tonnes from the upcoming harvest.
Advance payments to help production totalled 138 million hryvnias ($75 million), or 20.4 percent of a planned 675 million hryvnias ($365 million).
Only six percent of payments were made in cash, while 29 percent were in machinery, 30 percent in fertilisers and two percent in spare parts.
State contracts to buy feed grain, which should total 0.88 million tonnes, have not been concluded.

But in spite of the arrears and underpayments, farm producers have little choice but to opt for state contracts, due to a lack of alternative sources of input supplies and a deficit of working capital.

Ukraine's drought-hit 1996 net grain harvest was a record-low 25.4 million tonnes. The former Soviet republic has ambitiously targeted net output of 38 million tonnes this year -- a figure most believe to be unattainable.
